notes.front: What is Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)?
notes.back: A programme that offers free basic tax return preparation to qualified individuals.
notes.explanation: The programme has operated for over 50 years.
notes.example: Like a free tax clinic at a community centre, but run to national training and quality standards.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: The IRS's Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) programs offer free basic tax return preparation to qualified individuals. The VITA program has operated for over 50 years.

notes.front: What is Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE)?
notes.back: A free tax help programme, particularly for people aged 60 and older, specialising in pensions and retirement questions.
notes.explanation: It runs in addition to VITA, and its speciality is the retirement-related issues unique to seniors.
notes.example: Like VITA’s free service, but with its expertise pointed at pension and retirement questions.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: In addition to VITA, the TCE program offers free tax help, particularly for those who are 60 years of age and older, specializing in questions about pensions and retirement-related issues unique to seniors.

notes.front: What is the mission of Stakeholder Partnerships, Education and Communication (SPEC)?
notes.back: To help taxpayers meet their tax responsibilities by building and maintaining partnerships with key stakeholders.
notes.explanation: It pursues that mission by informing, educating and communicating with the customers it shares with those stakeholders.
notes.example: Like a head office that works through local partners: SPEC headquarters and territory offices oversee partner-run VITA/TCE sites.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “SPEC Mission”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Stakeholder Partnerships, Education and Communication (SPEC) mission is to help taxpayers satisfy their tax responsibilities by building and maintaining partnerships with key stakeholders, seeking to create and share value by informing, educating, and communicating with our shared customers.

notes.front: What is Link & Learn Taxes (LLT)?
notes.back: The online system through which every VITA/TCE volunteer must register and certify.
notes.explanation: Its online tests give results immediately.
notes.example: Like an online driving-theory test centre, but for VITA/TCE certification, with the score shown at once.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-3
notes.evidence: All volunteers must register and certify via Link & Learn Taxes. The online tests are available at www.linklearncertification.com/. Online testing is fast and efficient; it provides test results immediately.

notes.front: What is the Practice Lab?
notes.back: A tax year 2025 tax preparation tool built to help VITA/TCE volunteers through certification.
notes.explanation: Reaching it needs a universal password, which an instructor, site coordinator or other volunteer contact provides.
notes.example: Like a flight simulator for tax software: volunteers practise the test returns before certifying.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Using Tax Preparation Software”, p. 2
notes.evidence: The Practice Lab is a tax year 2025 tax preparation tool developed to help in the certification process for VITA/TCE volunteers. Select Practice Lab from the VITA/TCE Springboard. A universal password will be needed to access the Practice Lab. Your instructor, Site Coordinator, or other VITA/TCE volunteer contact will be able to provide you with the universal password.

notes.front: In VITA/TCE training, what is a certification level?
notes.back: A tier of tax law certification: each certification path and each optional specialty course in the training guide represents one.
notes.explanation: The first six lessons apply to all levels; later lessons carry icons marking the level each subject belongs to.
notes.example: Like grades of a driving licence: the same basics for everyone, then extra entitlements for higher grades.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How is the course structured?”, p. 1-2
notes.evidence: There are two tax law certification paths and two optional specialty courses presented in this publication, each representing a level of certification. The first six lessons apply to all levels of certification. Beginning with the Income lessons, the course levels for the subject being covered will be indicated by the following icons:

notes.front: What does Basic certification cover?
notes.back: The completion of wage-earner type returns.
notes.explanation: Link & Learn Taxes adds that Social Security income and the penalty on early withdrawal of savings are part of the Basic course.
notes.example: Like a licence for the everyday returns: wages, some Social Security, a savings penalty, but not the harder topics.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Course descriptions”
notes.evidence: Basic: Covers the completion of wage earner type returns. Social Security income and penalty on early withdrawal of savings is part of the Basic course.

notes.front: What does Advanced certification cover?
notes.back: The completion of the full scope of returns.
notes.explanation: Link & Learn Taxes says this includes capital gains and losses and more complex pension issues.
notes.example: Like the full licence: everything Basic covers, plus topics such as capital gains and harder pension questions.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Course descriptions”
notes.evidence: Advanced: Covers the completion of the full scope of returns. Includes capital gains and losses and more complex pension issues.

notes.front: In VITA/TCE certification, what is the retest?
notes.back: The version of an exam presented on the second attempt, after a volunteer fails the first.
notes.explanation: Both the test and the retest come from Form 6744, whose scenarios are the same as those online.
notes.example: Like a resit paper: same subject and format, but presented only once the first sitting has been failed.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Taking VITA/TCE Certification Tests”, p. 13
notes.evidence: The test scenarios on VITA/TCE Central are the same as in the printed test booklet (Form 6744, VITA/ TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest). Volunteers taking the test will be presented with the test from the 6744. If volunteers fail an exam, the retest will be presented on the second attempt.

notes.front: What is the Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement (Form 13615)?
notes.back: The form every VITA/TCE volunteer signs and dates before working at a site, after passing the Volunteer Standards of Conduct certification.
notes.explanation: The form also records the volunteer’s certification.
notes.example: Like a signed code of conduct for a new job, but it also carries the holder’s certification results.
notes.source: Form 13615 (Rev. 10-2025), Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement – VITA/TCE Programs, “Use of Form 13615”, p. 1
notes.evidence: Use of Form 13615: This form provides information on a volunteer's certification. All VITA/TCE volunteers must pass the Volunteer Standards of Conduct certification, and sign and date Form 13615, Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement - VITA/TCE Programs, prior to working at a VITA/TCE site.

notes.front: What is the Volunteer Protection Act (VPA)?
notes.back: Public Law 105-19 of 1997, which generally protects volunteers from liability for negligent acts within the scope of their responsibilities.
notes.explanation: It is a public law for any organisation that uses volunteers, not one written only for the Internal Revenue Service.
notes.example: Like a shield for volunteers in any charity, but it covers only what they do within their role.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Volunteer Protection Act”, p. 17
notes.evidence: Public Law 105-19, Volunteer Protection Act of 1997 (VPA) generally protects volunteers from liability for negligent acts they perform within the scope of their responsibilities in the organization for whom they volunteer. The VPA is not owned or written exclusively for Internal Revenue Service. This is a public law and relates to organizations that use volunteers to provide services.

notes.front: In VITA/TCE, what does scope of service refer to?
notes.back: The VITA/TCE tax law topics applied to a volunteer-prepared return. It does not refer to income levels.
notes.explanation: Volunteers must spot out-of-scope returns early in preparation.
notes.example: Like a clinic that treats listed conditions only: what decides is the topic on the return, not the size of the income.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #1, Certification: VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Volunteers must spot out-of-scope returns early in the tax return preparation process. Refer all out-of-scope tax returns to a professional tax return preparer. Scope refers to VITA/TCE tax law topics applied to a volunteer prepared tax return. Scope does not refer to income levels.

notes.front: In VITA/TCE, when is a form or topic out of scope?
notes.back: When the form or schedule is not listed, because no training has been provided, or when the volunteer has not been trained on it.
notes.explanation: Many out-of-scope forms and schedules still appear on the list as reference.
notes.example: Like a menu listing dishes the kitchen no longer makes, marked as unavailable; anything not on the menu is not served at all.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: Many forms and schedules that are out of scope are included as reference. If a form or schedule is not listed, it is out of scope because no training has been provided. In addition, if a volunteer has not been trained on an in-scope tax law topic, that topic is out of scope for that volunteer.

notes.front: What is the Scope of Service chart?
notes.back: Publication 4012’s list of forms and topics, with columns for In Scope?, Scope Limitations and Certification Levels.
notes.explanation: Column 3 (In Scope?) does not stand alone: columns 4 and 5 can add topics or levels that change the answer.
notes.example: Like a menu with footnotes: a dish can be listed, yet a footnote limits who may order it.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: When using the list, please note that column 3 (In Scope?) does not stand alone. Additional information contained in columns 4 and 5 (Scope Limitations and Certification Levels) may include topics or

notes.front: Is there a programme-wide income limit for VITA?
notes.back: No. The Internal Revenue Service sets none, but individual VITA sites may set their own.
notes.explanation: The programme generally focuses on taxpayers who meet the earned income credit’s income guidelines.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: While the IRS does not set a program-wide income limit, individual VITA sites may establish their own. The program generally focuses on serving taxpayers who meet the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) income guidelines.

notes.front: Which income guide figure does the free tax preparation page give for people VITA sites help?
notes.back: People who generally make about $70,244 or less.
notes.explanation: The same list also names persons with disabilities and limited English-speaking taxpayers.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: Many sites offer free tax help to people who need assistance in preparing their own tax returns, including: People who generally make about $ 70,244 or less Persons with disabilities Limited English-speaking taxpayers

notes.front: Who manages the VITA and TCE programmes, and who operates the sites?
notes.back: The Internal Revenue Service manages the programmes; its partners operate the sites, which volunteers staff.
notes.explanation: The certified volunteers are often retired people linked to non-profit organisations that receive grants from the Internal Revenue Service.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: While the IRS manages the VITA and TCE programs, the VITA/TCE sites are operated by IRS partners and staffed by volunteers who want to make a difference in their communities. The IRS-certified volunteers who provide tax counseling are often retired individuals associated with non-profit organizations that receive grants from the IRS.

notes.front: Besides certifying volunteers’ tax law knowledge, what check must every VITA/TCE return pass before filing?
notes.back: A quality review.
notes.explanation: The requirement covers every return prepared at a VITA/TCE site, not a sample.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: In addition to requiring volunteers to certify their knowledge of the tax laws, the IRS requires a quality review check for every return prepared at a VITA/TCE site prior to filing.

notes.front: A taxpayer earning a little over the page’s income guide figure is told by a friend that VITA is legally barred from helping anyone above it. What is accurate?
notes.back: B: no programme-wide limit exists; individual sites may set their own.
notes.choices:
A) The friend is right: the figure is a programme-wide limit
B) There is no programme-wide limit, though a particular site may set its own
C) Only TCE may help taxpayers above the figure
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: the page says no programme-wide income limit is set, and gives the figure as “about”. C is wrong: nothing limits higher incomes to TCE.
notes.explanation: The page gives the figure only as a guide to whom many sites help.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: While the IRS does not set a program-wide income limit, individual VITA sites may establish their own.

notes.front: TCE offers free tax help particularly for people aged {{c1::60}} years and older.
notes.explanation: Its speciality is questions about pensions and retirement-related issues unique to seniors.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: the TCE program offers free tax help, particularly for those who are 60 years of age and older, specializing in questions about pensions and retirement-related issues unique to seniors.

notes.front: A 72-year-old widower wants free help with questions about his pension distributions. Which programme specialises in exactly this?
notes.back: A: Tax Counseling for the Elderly.
notes.choices:
A) Tax Counseling for the Elderly
B) The Practice Lab
C) Link & Learn Taxes
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are volunteer training and certification tools, not services for taxpayers.
notes.explanation: TCE focuses on people aged 60 and older and specialises in pension and retirement questions.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”, “Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers”
notes.evidence: the TCE program offers free tax help, particularly for those who are 60 years of age and older, specializing in questions about pensions and retirement-related issues unique to seniors.

notes.front: What is the mission of the VITA/TCE return preparation programmes?
notes.back: To help eligible taxpayers meet their tax responsibilities by providing free tax return preparation.
notes.explanation: To establish the greatest public trust, volunteers must keep the highest ethical standards and give quality service.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Volunteer Standards of Conduct”, p. -1
notes.evidence: The mission of the VITA/TCE return preparation programs is to assist eligible taxpayers in satisfying their tax responsibilities by providing free tax return preparation. To establish the greatest degree of public trust, volunteers are required to maintain the highest standards of ethical conduct and provide quality service.

notes.front: How many certification courses does Link & Learn Taxes provide?
notes.back: Six, plus a refresher course for returning volunteers.
notes.explanation: The training prepares VITA/TCE partners and volunteers to give quality return preparation in their communities.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Linking volunteers to quality e-learning solutions”
notes.evidence: Link & Learn Taxes is the web-based program providing six certification courses for volunteers and a refresher course for returning volunteers. This training prepares Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) partners and volunteers to provide quality tax return preparation services in their local communities.

notes.front: A volunteer who will only greet taxpayers asks whether she can skip registering in Link & Learn Taxes. What is the answer?
notes.back: B: all volunteers must register and certify through Link & Learn Taxes.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: only return preparers register
B) No: all volunteers must register and certify through Link & Learn Taxes
C) Yes, if her coordinator vouches for her
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: the rule covers all volunteers, not only preparers. C is wrong: a coordinator cannot waive it.
notes.explanation: They must also generate Form 13615 and give it to their site coordinator before volunteering.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Instructions for Completing Training, Certifications, and the VSC Agreement”, p. 18
notes.evidence: All volunteers are required to register and certify via Link & Learn Taxes (LLT). Volunteers must generate the Form 13615, Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement and provide to their Site Coordinator prior to volunteering.

notes.front: A returning volunteer plans to work the 2025 test returns in last year’s software. What is the problem?
notes.back: B: prior-year software will not give the correct answers for the 2025 test.
notes.choices:
A) None: any year’s software gives the same answers
B) Prior-year software will not generate the correct answers for the 2025 test
C) Last year’s software is allowed if the volunteer rounds the answers
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong: Form 6744 says prior-year software will not generate the correct answers, and rounding does not fix that.
notes.explanation: Volunteers using the Practice Lab should also check TaxSlayer’s blog that all 2025 calculation updates have been made.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Using Tax Preparation Software”, p. 2
notes.evidence: Using prior year software will not generate the correct answers for the 2025 test. When using the Practice Lab to prepare return preparation scenarios, check TaxSlayer's blog to ensure all 2025 updates to calculations have been made.

notes.front: Which exam is a prerequisite to every other VITA/TCE course?
notes.back: The Volunteer Standards of Conduct exam.
notes.explanation: A volunteer who has not passed it after the second attempt may not go on to any other exam.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Volunteer Standards of Conduct Training and Test”, p. 10
notes.evidence: Note: The Volunteer Standards of Conduct Exam is a prerequisite to all other courses. If you do not pass this exam after the second attempt, you may not proceed to any other exams.

notes.front: Which two tests must a volunteer pass before the Basic or Advanced test can be opened?
notes.back: The Volunteer Standards of Conduct test and the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 makes both a gate to the tax law tests.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: You must pass the Volunteer Standards of Conduct and Intake/Interview and Quality Review tests prior to accessing the Basic or Advanced certification test.

notes.front: A new volunteer has passed the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test and wants to go straight to the Advanced test. What must she do first?
notes.back: B: pass the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing more: she can open the Advanced test now
B) Pass the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test
C) Pass the Basic test
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: no other exam opens until both gate tests are passed. C is wrong: Basic is not required before Advanced.
notes.explanation: Publication 5378 says no other exam can be taken without first passing both the conduct exam and the Intake/Interview and Quality Review exam.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Intake/Interview & Quality Review Exam”, p. 11
notes.evidence: It is not possible to take any of the other exams without first passing both the VSOC exam and the Intake/ Interview and Quality Review exam.

notes.front: A volunteer fails the Volunteer Standards of Conduct exam on both attempts. Can he go on to take the Basic exam?
notes.back: B: after failing on the second attempt, he may not proceed to any other exam.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, Basic is a separate exam
B) No: after failing it on the second attempt, he may not proceed to any other exam
C) Yes, after a third attempt at the conduct exam
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: the conduct exam is a prerequisite to all other courses. C is wrong: volunteers have two attempts, not three.
notes.explanation: Publication 5378 makes the conduct exam the gate to everything else.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Volunteer Standards of Conduct Training and Test”, p. 10
notes.evidence: Note: The Volunteer Standards of Conduct Exam is a prerequisite to all other courses. If you do not pass this exam after the second attempt, you may not proceed to any other exams.

notes.front: Which VITA/TCE volunteers must take the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test?
notes.back: All volunteers, including those who do not prepare returns.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 lists it as Step 1 for everyone.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Step 1: Volunteer Standards of Conduct. This test is for all volunteers, including volunteers who do not prepare returns.

notes.front: A retired teacher will only welcome taxpayers at the door and show them to the waiting area, never discussing tax law. Which certification must she pass?
notes.back: B: the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test.
notes.choices:
A) None, because she gives no tax advice
B) The Volunteer Standards of Conduct test
C) The Basic tax law test
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: every volunteer must pass it. C is wrong: volunteers who do not help with tax law issues need no tax law certification.
notes.explanation: To take part in the VITA/TCE programmes at all, a volunteer must pass the conduct test.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-3
notes.evidence: To participate in the VITA/TCE programs, all volunteers must pass the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test.

notes.front: Which tax roles must pass the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test according to Publication 4491?
notes.back: Tax preparers, quality reviewers and instructors, as well as client facilitators and coordinators.
notes.explanation: This comes in addition to the conduct test that every volunteer passes.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: In addition, all tax preparers, quality reviewers, instructors, client facilitators and coordinators must pass the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test.

notes.front: Must a greeter who helps taxpayers complete Form 13614-C pass the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test?
notes.back: Yes, as must greeters, screeners and client facilitators who assign returns to preparers.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 extends the test beyond preparers to anyone who helps with Form 13614-C or assigns returns.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-2: Required Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Also, all instructors, coordinators, return preparers, quality reviewers and other volunteers including greeters, screeners and client facilitators who assist taxpayers in completing Form 13614-C, or assign tax returns to VITA/TCE preparers must pass the Intake/ Interview and Quality Review certification test.

notes.front: A screener decides which preparer gets each return but never answers tax law questions. What must she pass besides the conduct test?
notes.back: B: the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing else
B) The Intake/Interview and Quality Review test
C) The Advanced test
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: volunteers who assign returns must pass it. C is wrong: she answers no tax law questions, so tax law certification is not required of her.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 names screeners who assign returns to preparers.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-2: Required Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training”, p. 4
notes.evidence: other volunteers including greeters, screeners and client facilitators who assist taxpayers in completing Form 13614-C, or assign tax returns to VITA/TCE preparers must pass the Intake/ Interview and Quality Review certification test.

notes.front: Which volunteers must certify in tax law before doing tax law tasks?
notes.back: Those who answer tax law questions or teach tax law; and those who prepare, correct or quality review returns.
notes.explanation: The certification must be in place before any tax law related task is done.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Volunteers who answer tax law questions, instruct tax law classes, prepare, or correct tax returns, and/or conduct quality reviews of completed tax returns, must certify in tax law prior to conducting tax law related tasks.

notes.front: When must a site coordinator certify in tax law?
notes.back: When preparing returns, giving tax law help, correcting rejected returns or quality reviewing, to the level the returns need.
notes.explanation: A coordinator who does none of these duties need not certify in tax law.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #5, Volunteer Agreement”, p. 6
notes.evidence: Coordinators who prepare tax returns, provide tax law assistance, correct rejected returns, or quality review tax returns must certify in tax law to the level required for the complexity of the returns. If they do NOT perform any of these duties, they are not required to certify in tax law

notes.front: A site coordinator now fixes the site’s rejected e-filed returns herself. What does this require of her?
notes.back: B: tax law certification to the level the returns need.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing new: coordinators never need tax law certification
B) Tax law certification to the level the returns need
C) Only the Site Coordinator test
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: coordinators who correct rejected returns must certify in tax law. C is wrong: the coordinator test does not replace tax law certification.
notes.explanation: Correcting rejected returns is one of the duties that brings a coordinator under the tax law rule.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #5, Volunteer Agreement”, p. 6
notes.evidence: Coordinators who prepare tax returns, provide tax law assistance, correct rejected returns, or quality review tax returns must certify in tax law to the level required for the complexity of the returns.

notes.front: Must greeters, receptionists and equipment coordinators certify in tax law?
notes.back: No, but they must still complete the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test through Link & Learn Taxes.
notes.explanation: The tax law rule applies to volunteers who help with tax law related issues.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Volunteers who do not help with tax law related issues (for example, greeters, receptionists, equipment coordinators) do not have to certify in tax law but must still complete the VSC certification test via LLT.

notes.front: A volunteer will set up and look after the site’s laptops and printers and never discuss tax. Which is right?
notes.back: A: the conduct test, but no tax law certification.
notes.choices:
A) He needs the conduct test but no tax law certification
B) He needs Basic certification because he handles taxpayer data
C) He needs no certification of any kind
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: equipment coordinators do not have to certify in tax law. C is wrong: they must still complete the conduct test.
notes.explanation: Publication 4961 names equipment coordinators among volunteers who do not help with tax law issues.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Volunteers who do not help with tax law related issues (for example, greeters, receptionists, equipment coordinators) do not have to certify in tax law but must still complete the VSC certification test via LLT.

notes.front: What minimum score passes any VITA/TCE certification test?
notes.explanation: The same minimum applies to every certification test, tax law or not.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: Alternatively, you may certify at the Advanced level. You are not required to certify in Basic before taking the Advanced test. A minimum score of 80% is required to pass any certification test.

notes.front: A volunteer scores 11 of 15 on the Site Coordinator test. Has she passed?
notes.back: B: no; 80% of 15 is 12.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: 11 of 15 is over two-thirds
B) No: she needed 80%, which is 12 of 15
C) Yes, because coordinator tests have no pass mark
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: two-thirds is below the 80% minimum. C is wrong: coordinators must pass with 80% or higher.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 sets the Site Coordinator minimum at 12 out of 15 correct.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests (cont’d)”, p. 5
notes.evidence: Site Coordinator. Estimated completion time: 1 hour. Minimum proficiency required: 12 out of 15 correct.

notes.front: How many attempts does a volunteer have to pass each certification?
notes.back: Two, each needing a score of 80% or above.
notes.explanation: Publication 4961 states the rule under the certification requirement.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #1, Certification”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Volunteers have two attempts to pass each certification with a passing score of 80% or above on each certification.

notes.front: After failing the Intake/Interview and Quality Review exam, the volunteer may review the training and try again; the questions may be {{c1::different}} on the second attempt.
notes.back: Different.
notes.explanation: Before that second attempt, the volunteer may review the training.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Intake/Interview & Quality Review Exam”, p. 11
notes.evidence: If you fail the exam, you may review the Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training and take the exam again. The exam questions may be different on the second attempt.

notes.front: A volunteer fails the Basic test, reviews the course, and fails the Basic retest. What is the position?
notes.back: B: both attempts are used, and he has not certified in Basic.
notes.choices:
A) He may keep retaking Basic until he passes
B) His two attempts at Basic are used up; he has not certified in Basic
C) He is certified in Basic because he completed both attempts
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: volunteers have two attempts per certification. C is wrong: certifying needs a passing score of 80%.
notes.explanation: Each certification allows two attempts, each needing 80%.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Taking VITA/TCE Certification Tests”, p. 13
notes.evidence: Site coordinators must achieve a passing score of 80% or higher prior to the site opening. You are allowed two attempts to take each exam.

notes.front: How many questions must a volunteer get right on the Volunteer Standards of Conduct test, and out of how many?
notes.back: Eight out of ten.
notes.explanation: Eight of ten is the 80% minimum; Form 6744 estimates an hour to complete it.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Step 1: Volunteer Standards of Conduct. This test is for all volunteers, including volunteers who do not prepare returns. Estimated completion time: 1 hour. Minimum proficiency required: 8 out of 10 correct.

notes.front: A new volunteer answers 7 of the 10 Volunteer Standards of Conduct questions correctly. What follows?
notes.back: B: he fails (8 of 10 needed) and may use his second attempt.
notes.choices:
A) He passes: 7 is a majority
B) He fails and may use his second attempt
C) He passes, but only for non-tax roles
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: the minimum is 8 out of 10. C is wrong: there is no lower pass mark for non-tax roles.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 sets the minimum at 8 out of 10 correct.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Minimum proficiency required: 8 out of 10 correct. Step 2: Intake/Interview and Quality Review.

notes.front: On the Intake/Interview and Quality Review test, how many correct answers out of how many are needed?
notes.back: Eight out of ten.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 estimates the test at 20 minutes, and it is for tax law certified volunteers, site coordinators, quality reviewers and instructors.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Step 2: Intake/Interview and Quality Review. This test is for all tax law certified volunteers, site coordi- nators, quality reviewers, and instructors. Estimated completion time: 20 minutes. Minimum proficiency required: 8 out of 10 correct.

notes.front: A quality reviewer answers 8 of the 10 Intake/Interview and Quality Review questions correctly. Has she passed?
notes.back: A: yes; 8 of 10 is the minimum.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: 8 of 10 is the minimum
B) No: 9 of 10 is needed
C) No: quality reviewers need 100%
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong: Form 6744 sets the minimum at 8 out of 10 correct for everyone taking this test.
notes.explanation: Eight of ten meets the 80% pass mark exactly.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Intake/Interview & Quality Review Exam”, p. 11
notes.evidence: You must pass the 10-question exam with a score of 80% or greater.

notes.front: How many correct answers does the Basic test require, out of how many questions?
notes.back: 24 out of 30.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 recommends Basic for, but does not limit it to, volunteers with 0–1 years of experience.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests (cont’d)”, p. 5
notes.evidence: Basic. Recommended for, but not limited to, volunteers with 0-1 years of experience. Estimated completion time: 4 hours. Minimum proficiency required: 24 out of 30 correct.

notes.front: A first-year volunteer gets 23 of the 30 Basic questions right. What is her result?
notes.back: B: fail; 24 of 30 is the minimum.
notes.choices:
A) Pass: 23 is more than three-quarters
B) Fail: she needed 24 of 30
C) Pass, because first-year volunteers have a lower mark
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: 23 of 30 is under 80%. C is wrong: the experience guide is a recommendation, not a different pass mark.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 sets the Basic minimum at 24 out of 30 correct.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests (cont’d)”, p. 5
notes.evidence: Minimum proficiency required: 24 out of 30 correct.

notes.front: How many correct answers does the Advanced test require, out of how many questions?
notes.back: 28 out of 35.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 recommends Advanced for, but does not limit it to, volunteers with two or more years of experience.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Certification Tests (cont’d)”, p. 5
notes.evidence: Advanced. Recommended for, but not limited to, volunteers with two or more years of experience. Estimated completion time: 4 hours. Minimum proficiency required: 28 out of 35 correct.

notes.front: A volunteer scores 28 of 35 on the Advanced test. What is his result?
notes.back: A: pass; 28 of 35 is the minimum.
notes.choices:
A) Pass: 28 of 35 is exactly the minimum
B) Fail: 30 of 35 is needed
C) Fail: Advanced needs 90%
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong: Form 6744 sets the Advanced minimum at 28 out of 35, which is 80%.
notes.explanation: The Advanced answer sheet shows 35 questions and a passing score of 28.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Advanced Test Answer Sheet”, p. 7
notes.evidence: Total Questions: 35 19. Passing Score: 28 of 35

notes.front: May volunteers use reference material during the certification test?
notes.back: Yes. It is open book: the course book and any reference material they will use as a volunteer.
notes.explanation: A draft Form 13614-C is included in the return preparation scenarios for use with the test.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Reference Materials”, p. 2
notes.evidence: This is an open book test. You may use your course book and any other reference material you will use as a volunteer. A draft Form 13614-C, Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, is included in the return preparation scenarios.

notes.front: Two new volunteers plan to sit the Basic test side by side with Publication 4012 open and compare answers. Which part of the plan breaks the test rules?
notes.back: B: comparing answers; the test is open book but must be taken alone.
notes.choices:
A) Using Publication 4012
B) Comparing answers with each other
C) Both parts
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: reference material a volunteer will use at the site is allowed. C is wrong for the same reason.
notes.explanation: Form 6744 allows the course book and reference material, but not taking the test in groups.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Reference Materials”, p. 2
notes.evidence: This is an open book test. You may use your course book and any other reference material you will use as a volunteer.

notes.front: A volunteer prefers to take the test on paper using Form 6744. What must she then do?
notes.back: Transcribe her answers into Link & Learn Taxes.
notes.explanation: Transcribing meets the requirement that all volunteers register and certify through Link & Learn Taxes.
notes.source: Form 6744 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test/Retest, “Taking the Test”, p. 3
notes.evidence: volunteers who prefer to take the certi- fication test on paper utilizing Form 6744, VITA/TCE Volunteer Assistor’s Test or Retest, may continue to complete the test using this method but must transcribe their answers to the test in Link & Learn Taxes to meet the requirement for all volunteers to register and certify through Link & Learn Taxes.

notes.front: How does Basic certification differ from Advanced certification in what it covers?
notes.back: Basic: wage-earner type returns. Advanced: the full scope of VITA/TCE returns.
notes.explanation: From the Income lessons on, icons show which of these levels each subject belongs to.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How is the course structured?”, p. 1-2
notes.evidence: Beginning with the Income lessons, the course levels for the subject being covered will be indicated by the following icons: Basic covers the completion of wage earner type returns. Advanced covers the completion of the full scope of VITA/TCE returns.

notes.front: Must a volunteer certify in Basic before taking the Advanced test?
notes.back: No. Basic and Advanced are standalone certifications.
notes.explanation: Publication 5378 says it is not required to take Basic to certify in Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Taking VITA/TCE Certification Tests”, p. 13
notes.evidence: Volunteers preparing tax returns must pass either the Basic or Advanced certification test. Note that Basic and Advanced are standalone certifications; it is not required to take the Basic exam if you wish to certify in Advanced.

notes.front: A new volunteer who works as a bookkeeper has passed both gate tests and wants to certify at Advanced without taking Basic. Is that allowed?
notes.back: A: yes; Basic is not a prerequisite for Advanced.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: Basic is not required before Advanced
B) No: Basic must always come first
C) Only with the coordinator’s written approval
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: the two are standalone certifications. C is wrong: no approval is needed.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 lets a volunteer pass Basic or, alternatively, certify at Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: To prepare tax returns in the VITA/TCE programs, you must then pass at least the Basic certification test. Alternatively, you may certify at the Advanced level. You are not required to certify in Basic before taking the Advanced test.

notes.front: What is the minimum tax law certification needed to prepare returns in VITA/TCE?
notes.back: Basic (or, alternatively, Advanced).
notes.explanation: Advanced is the alternative route to the same permission.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: To prepare tax returns in the VITA/TCE programs, you must then pass at least the Basic certification test. Alternatively, you may certify at the Advanced level.

notes.front: Which returns may a certified volunteer preparer prepare?
notes.back: Only returns whose tax issues fall within the preparer’s certification level.
notes.explanation: If a site prepares returns above Basic, its preparers must certify to the level those returns need.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #1, Certification”, p. 4
notes.evidence: IRS tax law certified volunteer preparers can only prepare returns with tax issues that fall within their certification level. If the site is preparing tax returns above the Basic certification level, the volunteer preparer must certify to the level needed to prepare these returns.

notes.front: A Basic-certified quality reviewer is handed a return that needed Advanced certification to prepare. What should happen?
notes.back: B: a reviewer certified to the needed level reviews it.
notes.choices:
A) She reviews it: any certified reviewer may review any return
B) A reviewer certified to the level the return needs reviews it
C) The preparer reviews his own return instead
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: reviewers may only review returns within their certification level. C is wrong: self review is not allowed.
notes.explanation: Every return must be quality reviewed by another volunteer certified to the level the return requires.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #2, Intake/Interview and Quality Review Process”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Self Review is not allowed. All returns must be quality reviewed by another volunteer certified to the level required for the return.

notes.front: A Basic-certified preparer’s client needs a Schedule D. What should the preparer do?
notes.back: B: refer it to an Advanced-certified volunteer or a site preparing at that level.
notes.choices:
A) Prepare it anyway; Schedule D is in scope
B) Pass the return to a volunteer certified at Advanced, or a site that prepares at that level
C) Leave Schedule D off the return
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: in scope for the programme is not the same as within this volunteer’s level. C is wrong: leaving it off makes the return incomplete.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 sends returns beyond a volunteer’s level to a volunteer or site certified for it.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, p. 6
notes.evidence: If the tax return does not fall within the volunteer’s certification level, refer the taxpayer to another IRS-tax law certified volunteer preparer with the appropriate certification level or to another site that prepares returns at that certification level.

notes.front: Which certification must a volunteer hold before taking the Military specialty test?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Link & Learn Taxes describes Military as an optional specialty course covering members of the Armed Forces, Reserve and National Guard.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Course descriptions”
notes.evidence: Military (optional specialty course): Covers the full scope of returns presented by members of the Armed Forces, Reserve and National Guard. To take this course, you must first be certified in the "Advanced" course module.

notes.front: The International specialty course covers taxpayers living outside the United States. What must a volunteer be certified in before taking it?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The course includes the foreign income exclusion and the foreign tax credit.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Course descriptions”
notes.evidence: It includes the Foreign Income Exclusion and Foreign Tax Credit. To take this course, you must first be certified in the "Advanced" course module.

notes.front: Which certification must a volunteer hold before taking the Puerto Rico specialty certification?
notes.back: Basic or Advanced.
notes.explanation: Military and International, by contrast, require Advanced first.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Specialty Certifications”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Volunteers must first certify at either Basic or Advanced level before taking the specialty certification for Puerto Rico. ◦ Volunteers must first certify at the Advanced level before taking the Military and International specialty certifications.

notes.front: Which exam is the prerequisite for the Over-the-Phone Interpreter course?
notes.back: Only the Volunteer Standards of Conduct exam.
notes.explanation: Unlike the other course tabs, it does not also link the Intake/Interview and Quality Review exam.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Volunteer Standards of Conduct Training and Test”, p. 9
notes.evidence: All tabs include a link to the VSOC exam and Intake/Interview and Quality Review exam except for Over-the-Phone Interpreter, which has only the VSOC exam as a prerequisite.

notes.front: At what level must tax law instructors certify?
notes.back: Advanced, plus an applicable specialty course depending on the topics taught.
notes.explanation: The specialty needed follows the subjects the instructor will teach.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: Volunteer instructors must certify at Advanced and an applicable specialty course, depending on the tax topics instructed.

notes.front: A Basic-certified volunteer with years of site experience is asked to teach this season’s tax law class. What must happen first?
notes.back: B: he must certify at Advanced, plus any applicable specialty course.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing: experience counts instead of certification
B) He must certify at Advanced (plus any applicable specialty)
C) He must retake Basic
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: instructors must certify at Advanced or higher. C is wrong: Basic is below the instructor level.
notes.explanation: Tax law instructors must hold Advanced or higher.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #1, Certification”, p. 4
notes.evidence: Tax law instructors must certify in tax law at the Advanced level or higher.

notes.front: May a partner set training requirements different from SPEC’s?
notes.back: Yes, higher ones, but partner requirements can never be lower than those of the Internal Revenue Service.
notes.explanation: Publication 4961 gives partners that require Advanced certification of their coordinators as an example.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Specialty Certifications”, p. 4
notes.evidence: SPEC requirements may be different from partner requirements. Partners may require a higher level of training. However, partner requirements can never be lower than IRS requirements. For example, some partners require their coordinators to be certified at the Advanced tax law certification level, even if they do not give tax law advice, prepare, or correct tax returns.

notes.front: How often must a volunteer certify in tax law?
notes.back: Every year: it is an annual requirement.
notes.explanation: Screeners and client facilitators who answer tax law questions are covered by it as well.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Screeners and client facilitators who answer tax law questions must also certify in tax law. Tax law certification is an annual requirement.

notes.front: A preparer certified at Advanced last season returns this season and wants to start preparing on day one without testing. Which is right?
notes.back: B: she must pass this year’s tests, including tax law, first.
notes.choices:
A) Last season’s certification still covers her
B) She must pass this year’s tests, including tax law, first
C) She needs only to re-sign last year’s Form 13615
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: tax law certification is annual. C is wrong: Form 13615 is signed each year after that year’s certifications.
notes.explanation: Publication 4961 makes tax law certification an annual requirement.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Tax law certification is an annual requirement.

notes.front: Who must pass the Site Coordinator test, and when?
notes.back: All coordinators and alternate coordinators, with 80% or higher, before working at a site.
notes.explanation: The test is available on Link & Learn Taxes.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Instructions for Completing Training, Certifications, and the VSC Agreement”, p. 18
notes.evidence: All coordinators and alternate coordinators are now required to certify by passing the Site Coordinator Test with a score of 80% or higher prior to working at a site. The Site Coordinator test is available on LLT.

notes.front: What does Link & Learn Taxes add to Form 13615 after each passed test?
notes.back: The letter “P”, showing a passing score for that certification.
notes.explanation: This is how the form captures the volunteer’s certification level.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Reminders about certifying using Link & Learn Taxes”, p. 19
notes.evidence: After each test, the Link & Learn Taxes system on VITA/TCE Central will add the letter “P” to Form 13615 indicating a passing score for the VSC Training and (if applicable) Intake/Interview and Quality Review certification and tax law certification levels.

notes.front: What does Link & Learn Taxes fill in on Form 13615 automatically?
notes.back: All completed and passed exams (on page 2) and the details from the volunteer’s registration page.
notes.explanation: The sponsoring partner or site name and the approving official’s name and title can be completed by hand.
notes.source: Publication 5378 (Rev. 11-2025), Link & Learn Taxes Certification Tests: Getting Started, “Signing Your Form 13615, Volunteer Agreement”, p. 13
notes.evidence: All completed and passed exams are entered automatically on page 2 of the form. – All the information from your registration page will transfer to Form 13615. – The sponsoring partner/site name and approving official name and title can be manually completed by volunteers.

notes.front: A volunteer passed her tests online but has not yet signed Form 13615. She wants to start greeting taxpayers today. Which is right?
notes.back: B: she must sign and date Form 13615 before working at the site.
notes.choices:
A) She may start: passing the tests is enough
B) She must sign and date Form 13615 before working at the site
C) She may start if she signs by the end of the season
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong: the form must be signed and dated prior to working at a VITA/TCE site.
notes.explanation: Passing the conduct certification is only half of the requirement.
notes.source: Form 13615 (Rev. 10-2025), Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement – VITA/TCE Programs, “Use of Form 13615”, p. 1
notes.evidence: All VITA/TCE volunteers must pass the Volunteer Standards of Conduct certification, and sign and date Form 13615, Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement - VITA/TCE Programs, prior to working at a VITA/TCE site.

notes.front: When does a signed Form 13615 become valid?
notes.back: Once the approving official confirms the volunteer’s identity, name and address with government-issued photo identification, and signs and dates it.
notes.explanation: The approving official can be the coordinator, sponsoring partner, instructor or the agency’s contact.
notes.source: Form 13615 (Rev. 10-2025), Volunteer Standards of Conduct Agreement – VITA/TCE Programs, “Use of Form 13615”, p. 1
notes.evidence: This form is not valid until the coordinator, sponsoring partner, instructor, or IRS contact confirms the volunteer’s identity, name and address with a government-issued photo ID, and signs and dates this form.

notes.front: When must coordinators be able to verify a volunteer’s training certification?
notes.back: On the day the volunteer reports to the site.
notes.explanation: Coordinators must exercise due diligence and have a method for this check.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #5, Volunteer Agreement”, p. 6
notes.evidence: Coordinators must exercise due diligence and have a method to verify training certification the day the volunteer reports to the site.

notes.front: A volunteer emails her signed Form 13615 to the coordinator, who files it without meeting her or seeing any identification. Is the form valid?
notes.back: B: no; the official must check photo identification and sign and date it.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: the volunteer signed it
B) No: the official must confirm identity, name and address with government-issued photo identification and sign and date it
C) Yes, if the tests show “P”
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong: neither the volunteer’s signature nor passing scores make the form valid on their own.
notes.explanation: The official also verifies the volunteer’s certification level before signing.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Instructions for Completing Training, Certifications, and the VSC Agreement”, p. 18
notes.evidence: Form 13615 is not valid until it is signed and dated by the sponsoring partner, coordinator, instructor, or IRS contact, after verifying the volunteer’s identity, name and address (with government-issued photo ID) and certification level.

notes.front: Which names must match on a volunteer’s paperwork?
notes.back: The name on Form 13615 must match the photo identification and the name added to the tax software.
notes.explanation: SPEC does not allow volunteer nicknames in the tax preparation software.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “QSR #5, Volunteer Agreement”, p. 6
notes.evidence: The name on Form 13615 must match both the name on the government-issued photo ID and the volunteer’s name added to TaxSlayer or other tax preparation software. SPEC does not allow the use of volunteer nicknames in the tax preparation software.

notes.front: A volunteer does not reach the minimum score on the tax law test or the retest. What does Publication 4491 encourage?
notes.back: Taking part in another capacity, such as greeter, client facilitator, communication specialist or technical support.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 gives these as examples (“such as”), not a closed list.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: If a volunteer does not achieve the minimum required score on the test or the retest, the volunteer is encouraged to participate in the program in another capacity such as greeter, client facilitator, communication specialist, or technical support.

notes.front: Is the insert a coordinator may give certified volunteers (Form 14509) proof of certification?
notes.back: No. It is not intended to be used as proof of certification.
notes.explanation: It was created to acknowledge certified volunteers and to help internal and external stakeholders identify them.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “How does this certification work?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: The insert was created to acknowledge the accomplishment of certified volunteers, as well as to assist internal and external stakeholders in identifying certified volunteers, but is not intended to be used as proof of certification.

notes.front: Are VITA/TCE volunteers legally liable under federal law for the returns they prepare?
notes.back: No: they are not considered paid preparers.
notes.explanation: It also means they cannot accept payment of any kind for preparing a federal return or other tax help.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Am I legally liable for returns I prepare?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: VITA/TCE program volunteers are not considered paid preparers; therefore, you are not legally liable under federal law for the return you prepare. This means you cannot accept payment of any kind from the taxpayer for preparing a federal tax return or for providing any other tax-related assistance.

notes.front: A grateful taxpayer offers a volunteer $30 “for answering a few extra tax questions” after her return is done. Which is right?
notes.back: B: he must decline any payment for tax-related help.
notes.choices:
A) He may accept, since the return itself was free
B) He must decline: volunteers cannot accept payment of any kind for tax-related help
C) He may accept if he gives it to the site coordinator
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: the ban covers any other tax-related assistance, not just the return. C is wrong: handing it on is still accepting payment.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 ties the ban to volunteers not being paid preparers.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Am I legally liable for returns I prepare?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: VITA/TCE program volunteers are not considered paid preparers; therefore, you are not legally liable under federal law for the return you prepare. This means you cannot accept payment of any kind from the taxpayer for preparing a federal tax return or for providing any other tax-related assistance.

notes.front: Which Volunteer Protection Act condition concerns the volunteer’s role?
notes.back: The volunteer is acting within the scope of their volunteer responsibilities.
notes.explanation: All the conditions must be true for the protection to apply.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Am I legally liable for returns I prepare?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: You are protected by the federal Volunteer Protection Act of 1997, as long as all of the following conditions are true: • You are acting within the scope of your volunteer responsibilities.

notes.front: Which Volunteer Protection Act condition concerns training?
notes.back: The volunteer completed the level of training and certification required for preparing returns at their site.
notes.explanation: It sits with the scope and conduct conditions, all of which must hold.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Am I legally liable for returns I prepare?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: You completed the level of training and certification required for preparing tax returns at your site.

notes.front: Which Volunteer Protection Act condition concerns how the harm was caused?
notes.back: The harm was not caused by willful, criminal, reckless, grossly negligent, or consciously, flagrantly indifferent acts.
notes.explanation: The protection covers negligence, not these more serious kinds of conduct.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Am I legally liable for returns I prepare?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: The harm was not caused by willful, criminal, reckless, grossly negligent, or conscious, flagrantly indifferent acts.

notes.front: Within which three certification levels must a volunteer’s returns stay?
notes.back: Their own tax law certification level, their site’s certification level, and the level under the VITA/TCE programme.
notes.explanation: Publication 4961 points to the Scope of Service chart in Publication 4012 for more.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Volunteer Protection Act”, p. 17
notes.evidence: Volunteers must only prepare returns that are within their tax law certification level, their site’s certification level, and the level of certification under the VITA/TCE program. See the Scope of Service Chart in Publication 4012 for more information.

notes.front: A Basic-certified volunteer, with no one else free, prepares a return that needs Advanced. An error later harms the taxpayer. What is his position under the Volunteer Protection Act?
notes.back: B: at risk; he had not completed the certification the return required.
notes.choices:
A) Protected: he was helping in good faith
B) At risk: he lacked the training and certification the return needed
C) Protected, because the return was quality reviewed
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong: the protection applies only when all its conditions hold, including the required training and certification.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 says the Act protects volunteers only while they prepare returns within the programmes’ scope.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “What types of returns can I prepare?”, p. 1-4
notes.evidence: It is important that you assist only with returns, supporting schedules, and forms for which you have been trained and certified. You are protected by the federal Volunteer Protection Act of 1997 as long as you are only preparing returns within the scope of the VITA/TCE programs.

notes.front: What kinds of conduct does the Volunteer Protection Act not protect?
notes.back: Harm caused by willful or criminal misconduct, gross negligence, reckless misconduct, or conscious, flagrant indifference to the harmed person’s rights or safety.
notes.explanation: Protection also needs the volunteer to have been acting within the scope of the programme.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “What does the VPA do?”, p. 17
notes.evidence: The VPA protects volunteers from liabilities if they were acting within the scope of the program and harm was not caused by willful or criminal misconduct, gross negligence, reckless misconduct, conscious, flagrant indifference to the rights or safety of the individual harmed by the volunteer.

notes.front: If volunteers do their work while keeping to the standards of conduct, are they protected regardless of local and state law?
notes.back: Generally protected, but local and state laws must still be considered.
notes.explanation: Sponsoring organisations should ask their attorneys how the law protects their volunteers.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “Volunteer Protection Act”, p. 18
notes.evidence: In general, if volunteers are performing their responsibilities while adhering to the Volunteer Standards of Conduct, they are protected. However, local and state laws still must be considered. Sponsoring organizations should seek advice from their attorneys to determine how this law protects their volunteers.

notes.front: A certified volunteer, working within her level, knowingly inflates a credit on a return. Does the Volunteer Protection Act protect her?
notes.back: B: no; willful conduct is outside the protection.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: she was within her certification level
B) No: willful conduct is not protected
C) Yes, because volunteers are not paid preparers
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: staying within level is only one condition. C is wrong: not being a paid preparer does not cover willful acts.
notes.explanation: Willful conduct is the first kind Publication 4961 lists as unprotected.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “What does the VPA do?”, p. 17
notes.evidence: The VPA does not protect conduct that is willful or criminal, grossly negligent, reckless, or conduct that constitutes a conscious, flagrant indifference to the rights or safety of the individual harmed by the volunteer.

notes.front: Under the Volunteer Protection Act, how much may a “volunteer” receive for their services in a year?
notes.back: No more than $500 in total, as compensation or anything of value in place of it.
notes.explanation: Reasonable reimbursement or allowance for expenses actually incurred does not count as compensation.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “What is a volunteer?”, p. 17
notes.evidence: who does not receive for these services more than $500 total in a year from the organization or entity as: • Compensation (other than reasonable reimbursement or allowance for expenses actually incurred), or • Any other thing of value in lieu of compensation

notes.front: A taxpayer with high wages but only a Form W-2 asks for help. Is her return out of scope because of her income?
notes.back: B: scope is about tax law topics, not income.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: high income puts a return out of scope
B) No: scope refers to tax law topics, not income levels
C) Yes, unless she is over 60
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: scope does not refer to income levels. C is wrong: age does not decide scope.
notes.explanation: The return’s tax law topics, not the taxpayer’s earnings, decide whether it is in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4961 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Standards of Conduct – Ethics Training, “VITA/TCE Tax Law Training”, p. 3
notes.evidence: Scope refers to VITA/TCE tax law topics applied to a volunteer prepared tax return. Scope does not refer to income levels.

notes.front: When should a volunteer check that a return is within scope and the volunteer’s certification level?
notes.back: At the start, while completing the intake and interview process.
notes.explanation: Checking early means no taxpayer is wrongly turned away and no out-of-scope return is prepared.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, p. 6
notes.evidence: Verifying whether a taxpayer’s return can be prepared at the start of the intake and interview process ensures no taxpayer is erroneously turned away from the site or that an out-of-scope return is prepared when it should not be.

notes.front: A return is outside VITA/TCE scope. What should the volunteer tell the taxpayer, and what must he avoid?
notes.back: That they must seek a professional preparer; he must not suggest any specific preparer.
notes.explanation: Naming one would be a conflict of interest, including preparers linked to a volunteer or to the site.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, p. 6
notes.evidence: If the return is not within the scope of VITA/TCE, explain to the taxpayer they must seek assistance from a professional preparer. Avoid a conflict of interest by not suggesting any specific professional preparer. This includes professional preparers associated with a volunteer, any other specific individual, or organization connected to the VITA/TCE site.

notes.front: On the Scope of Service chart, what does it mean when no certification level is listed for a topic?
notes.back: The topic is in scope for all certification levels.
notes.explanation: Only a listed level narrows which volunteers may prepare that topic.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: If no certification level is listed, the topic is in scope for all certification levels.

notes.front: Wages on Form 1040 line 1 are in scope. Which certification does the Scope of Service chart require if the taxpayer has unreported tip income?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The line is in scope, yet this case needs a higher level than Basic.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: F 1040 1 Yes Wages, salaries, tips, etc. Advanced certification required for unreported tip income

notes.front: Capital gain or loss (Form 1040 line 7) is in scope. What level does the Scope of Service chart require when Schedule D or Form 8949 is needed?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The line is in scope, but the forms the return needs decide the level.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: Advanced certification if Schedule D or Form 8949 required

notes.front: According to the Scope of Service chart, when is the Form 1040 digital asset question in scope?
notes.back: When the taxpayer can check the No box.
notes.explanation: The limit turns on the answer the taxpayer can give to the question.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: In scope if taxpayers can check the No box.

notes.front: A volunteer sees “Y” in the In Scope? column for a line and starts preparing. What has he missed?
notes.back: B: columns 4 and 5 may add limitations or levels.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing: “Y” settles it
B) Columns 4 and 5, which may add limitations or certification levels
C) The taxpayer’s income level
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: column 3 does not stand alone. C is wrong: scope does not refer to income.
notes.explanation: Those columns can decide whether volunteers may or may not prepare the return.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, p. 6
notes.evidence: When using the Scope of Service chart in Publication 4012, please note that column 3 (titled: In Scope?) does not stand alone. Additional information contained in columns 4 and 5 (titled: Scope Limitations and Certification Levels) may include topics or additional certification levels that affect whether volunteers may or may not prepare the return

notes.front: Is a form that the Scope of Service chart does not list in scope?
notes.back: No: an unlisted form or schedule is out of scope, because no training has been provided on it.
notes.explanation: Listing a form does not make it in scope either: many out-of-scope forms are listed for reference.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, p. vi
notes.evidence: Many forms and schedules that are out of scope are included as reference. If a form or schedule is not listed, it is out of scope because no training has been provided.

notes.front: An Advanced-certified volunteer skipped the lesson on an in-scope topic and now meets a return that needs it. Is that topic in scope for him?
notes.back: B: no; untrained topics are out of scope for that volunteer.
notes.choices:
A) Yes: it is in scope for the programme
B) No: a topic he has not been trained on is out of scope for him
C) Yes, because Advanced covers the full scope
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong: scope also depends on the volunteer’s own training, not only the programme’s list.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 says this in its scope section too.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “1-4: VITA/TCE Program Scope of Service”, p. 6
notes.evidence: While completing the intake and interview process, verify that the tax return is within the scope of the VITA/ TCE program and the volunteer’s certification level. If a volunteer has not been trained on an in-scope tax law topic, that topic is out of scope for that volunteer.

notes.front: What does Publication 4491-X contain?
notes.back: Changes, revisions and additions to the October 2025 VITA/TCE training publications.
notes.explanation: The changes affect all the VITA/TCE courses.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Introduction”, p. 1
notes.evidence: This supplement contains changes, revisions, and additions to the October 2025 versions of the VITA/TCE training publications. These changes impact all of the VITA/TCE courses.

notes.front: Who must review Publication 4491-X, and before what?
notes.back: Preparers, before helping with tax law questions or preparing returns; quality reviewers, before doing quality reviews.
notes.explanation: Quality reviewers are named separately from preparers, with their own deadline.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Introduction”, p. 1
notes.evidence: VITA/TCE tax preparers must review this supple- ment before assisting taxpayers with tax law questions or preparing their returns. Quality reviewers must also review this document before performing quality reviews.

notes.front: Your printed Publication 4012 shows a standard deduction of $15,000 for a single filer. Publication 4491-X lists a change to that chart. Which figure do you use?
notes.back: B: $15,750, the corrected figure.
notes.choices:
A) $15,000, as printed
B) $15,750, as corrected by Publication 4491-X
C) Whichever the taxpayer prefers
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: 4491-X replaces $15,000 with $15,750 in that chart. C is wrong: the amount is set by law, not chosen.
notes.explanation: The supplement also replaces $30,000 with $31,500 and $22,500 with $23,625 in the same chart.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “2025 Publication 4012: Tab F, Deductions”, p. 2
notes.evidence: in the Standard Deduction Chart for Most People*, under the Their Standard Deduction is…..column, replace: F-3 $15,000 with $15,750 $30,000 with $31,500 $22,500 with $23,625

notes.front: Which volunteers may certify through the Circular 230 Federal Tax Law Update Test?
notes.back: Attorneys, enrolled agents and certified public accountants; the test is optional.
notes.explanation: It covers new provisions and tax law changes.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Federal tax law update test for Circular 230 professionals”
notes.evidence: The test covers new provisions and tax law changes. Volunteers with the professional designation of attorney, enrolled agent or certified public accountant have the option of certifying via the Circular 230 Federal Tax Law Update Test.

notes.front: What is the maximum number of continuing education credits a VITA/TCE volunteer can earn?
notes.explanation: Volunteers seeking the credits must meet tax law certification requirements through Link & Learn Taxes.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Continuing education credit”
notes.evidence: Volunteers can earn a maximum of 18 continuing education credits. All volunteers requesting continuing education credits are required to meet tax law certification requirements via Link and Learn Taxes.

notes.front: An enrolled agent wants continuing education credits for quality reviewing at a site, and the partner offers to pay her an hourly fee. Can she have both?
notes.back: B: no; volunteers seeking the credits cannot be compensated for the work.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, if she also meets certification requirements
B) No: volunteers seeking the credits cannot be paid for that work
C) Yes, if the fee is under $500
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong: certification is required but does not lift the ban on pay. C is wrong: the $500 figure is the Volunteer Protection Act’s definition, not a credit rule.
notes.explanation: The rule covers instructors, quality reviewers and return preparers.
notes.source: IRS.gov, “Link & Learn Taxes”, “Continuing education credit”
notes.evidence: Volunteers cannot be compensated for their work as instructors, quality reviewers, or tax return preparers if they are seeking CE credits.
